topic: Bayes' Theorem and Independence: Unlocking Predictive Probability
target_audience: University students (Introductory Statistics or Computer Science)

sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: The Probability Space
lecture_lines: Visualize the total probability space as a square.
Identify the sub-circle of math students, B.
Within B, highlight the Data Science subset, A.
Focusing on B shrinks our universe of interest.
We now measure A relative only to B.
animations: Fade in 'Omega' set as a large white circle. [Color: #FFFFFF]
Display dots representing elements within the circle. [Color: #FFCC00]
Highlight two distinct event subsets A and B. [Color: #FF0000, #00CCFF]
Animate an arrow showing the probability of event A. [Color: #FFFFFF]

sections.title: Defining Independence: Does B change A?
lecture_lines: Events are independent if B doesn't change A.
Knowing B gives zero new information about A.
animations: Show two sets A and B overlapping. [Color: #FFFFFF]
Highlight the intersection A intersect B. [Color: #FF00FF]
Flash text: 'P(A|B) = P(A intersect B) / P(B)'. [Color: #00FF00]

sections.title: Bayes' Theorem: The Logic of Reverse Prediction
lecture_lines: Bayes' Theorem helps update our prior beliefs.
We use P(A|B) to correct our understanding.
Prior P(A) is updated by evidence P(B).
The evidence tips our internal probability scale.
We reverse prediction using the correction formula.
animations: Display formula: P(A|B) = P(B|A) * P(A) / P(B). [Color: #FFFFFF]
Animate P(B|A) with a scaling effect. [Color: #FF9900]
Show the inverse relationship visually using mirrored boxes. [Color: #FFFFFF]

sections.title: Synthesis & Application: The Diagnostic Power
lecture_lines: Independence simplifies our Bayesian probability calculations.
Dependent events use the likelihood ratio to update.
Bayes' prevents panic by checking prior probabilities.
animations: Present a real-world clinical test scenario. [Color: #FFFFFF]
Visualize positive test results inside A and B. [Color: #FF0000]
Calculate final posterior probability using the theorem. [Color: #00FF00]
